title: The Treaty Quraysh Broke • The Fasting Army of Ten Thousand • The Cousin’s Return • The Fires of Marr al-Zahran

blocks.1: In the Treaty of Hudaybiyah the condition was that whichever tribe wished could stay with the Muslims, and whichever wished with Quraysh. The Khuza‘ah tribe was an ally of the Prophet {{1}}, Banu Bakr of Quraysh. One night in the eighth year of Hijrah Banu Bakr attacked Khuza‘ah, beside a well near Makkah. Quraysh gave them weapons, and a few, in the darkness of night, entered the fight themselves. The people of Khuza‘ah slipped into the boundary of the Haram, yet they did not get relief. ‘Amr ibn Salim of Khuza‘ah (RA) rushed to Madinah, stood in the mosque and asked for help in verse; we are your allies, yet they struck us down while we were in ruku‘ and sujud.{{2}}
blocks.2: Quraysh realised what they had done. They sent Abu Sufyan ibn Harb to Madinah to reaffirm the treaty anew. Abu Sufyan raised the matter before the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} did not answer a single word. He went to Abu Bakr (RA). Abu Bakr said, I cannot. He went to ‘Umar (RA). ‘Umar said, should I intercede for you? By Allah, even if I had nothing in my hand but a piece of wood, I would fight you with that. He went to ‘Ali (RA). There Fatimah (RA) was, and in front, little Hasan was playing. Abu Sufyan said, ‘Ali, will you intercede a little with Muhammad on my behalf? ‘Ali (RA) said, Abu Sufyan, the Prophet {{3}} has made a decision; I cannot spell it out. Then Abu Sufyan said to ‘Ali, what is to be done now? ‘Ali said, you are the chief of Banu Kinanah. You stand up and yourself declare protection among everyone, then go back to your home. Abu Sufyan asked, will this work? ‘Ali said, I do not think so. But what else can I do? Abu Sufyan stood in the mosque and announced, people, I declare protection among you. Then, mounting his camel, he went back to Makkah. Quraysh asked, what happened? He told them everything. They said, did Muhammad uphold it? He said, no. They said, then he was only playing with you!{{4}}
blocks.3: For the one who himself breaks his word, while running about to save the treaty, all doors are closed before him. Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Ali, none could do anything; because the Prophet {{1}} had by then already made the decision. Before breaking one’s word it is good to remember this day, the day when you will have to come back and say, what can be done now? The treaty for which at Hudaybiyah the Prophet {{2}} had returned Abu Jandal in chains, Quraysh did not let even two years pass; they themselves broke it. The one who keeps his word, in the end time stands on his side; the one who breaks his word demolishes his own wall with his own hand.
blocks.4: The Fasting Army of Ten Thousand
blocks.5: The Prophet {{1}} prepared quietly. In the month of Ramadan he set out with ten thousand Companions; eight and a half years after coming to Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.6: The preparation was so secret that even ‘A’ishah (RA) did not know where the Prophet {{1}} was going. The Prophet {{2}} had said to her, keep the household things in order. Abu Bakr (RA) came and asked his daughter, my daughter, what is this preparation for? ‘A’ishah said, by Allah, I do not know. Abu Bakr said, this is not the time for fighting Banu al-Asfar! Then where will he go? ‘A’ishah said, that I too have not yet been able to find out. So that people would think the expedition was elsewhere, the Prophet {{3}} sent a small party of eight under Abu Qatadah ibn Rib‘i (RA) in another direction. The news of that party spread all around. The real party was by then on the road to Makkah.{{4}}
blocks.7: Even in the work of truth not everything has to be told to everyone. The work for which the Prophet {{1}} had waited two years, even its preparation he kept hidden for a few days. Staying silent until the right time is part of wisdom itself. One Badri Companion had wanted to send news of the preparation to Makkah in a secret letter; that incident and the Prophet’s {{2}} forgiveness came in Dars 15. Everyone was travelling while fasting. Reaching a spring called Kadid the Prophet {{3}} asked for a vessel of water, held it up so everyone could see, and then drank in the daytime itself. After that, until reaching Makkah, he did not fast again.{{4}}
blocks.8: Allah had given the concession of not fasting on a journey. Yet many were fasting with difficulty. The Prophet {{1}} himself broke his fast and showed it before everyone, so that no one would feel shy to take the concession. For one who is a leader, one action of his lightens the hardship of many.
blocks.10: On the road to Makkah, at a place called Thaniyyat al-‘Uqab, two men wished to meet the Prophet {{1}}. One was Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, the Prophet’s {{2}} cousin; for twenty years he had satirised him in verse. The other was ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, a paternal aunt’s son, brother of Umm Salamah (RA); in Makkah he had said hard words to him. Umm Salamah (RA) interceded, O Messenger of Allah, your cousin, your aunt’s son, your relative. The Prophet {{3}} said, I have no need of them. The cousin tore my honour to pieces; the aunt’s son said in Makkah what he said. The news reached Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith. With him was a son of his. He said, by Allah, either he will let me come, or I will take this boy’s hand and set out, go wherever I please, until I die of hunger or thirst. Hearing this, the Prophet’s {{4}} heart softened. He called the two in. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith (RA) came and said the very words of the brothers of Yusuf (AS), as the Qur’an has related it thus,
blocks.12: By Allah! Allah has favoured you over us, and we were certainly sinners.{{1}}
blocks.13: The Prophet {{1}} replied in the words of Yusuf (AS), as the Qur’an says it thus,
blocks.15: No blame will be brought against you today. May Allah forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of all the merciful.{{1}}
blocks.16: Then he recited a poem of his Islam and repentance. At one place he said, the day I carried the banner to make Lat’s horse win over Muhammad’s horse, I was a bewildered traveller on a dark night; today I have found the path. It was not I who guided me, someone else did; the one who brought me to Allah is that man whom I had driven away from every place. The Prophet {{1}} slapped him on the chest and said, you are the one who drove me out from every place!{{2}}
blocks.17: Twenty years of satire, all of it remembered; so at first he had even turned him away. But hearing of going out with his son’s hand to die, he could not hold out. At the time of forgiving he did not deny the hurt; he said this too, you are the one who drove me out, yet he drew him to his chest. To forgive does not mean to forget; it is to let go while remembering.
blocks.19: The army halted at Marr al-Zahran, close to Makkah. The Prophet {{1}} commanded, each of you light a separate fire. The valley filled with the fires of ten thousand people. Quraysh still knew nothing. Coming out to get news was Quraysh’s chief Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, with Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa’. Seeing the fires Abu Sufyan said, what is this! It is like the fires of ‘Arafah! Budayl said, it must be the fires of Banu ‘Amr. Abu Sufyan said, Banu ‘Amr are far fewer than this. The guards of the Prophet {{2}} saw them and brought them in. Abu Sufyan (RA) accepted Islam right there.{{3}}
blocks.20: The Prophet {{1}} said to ‘Abbas (RA), make Abu Sufyan stand in the narrow mountain pass, so that he sees the army’s passing with his own eyes. One by one the tribes began to pass, each with its own banner; Ghifar, Juhaynah, Sa‘d ibn Hudhaym, Sulaym. Each time Abu Sufyan asks, who are these? ‘Abbas (RA) says the name. Abu Sufyan says, what quarrel did I have with these! Then came such a band as Abu Sufyan had never seen before; the band of the Ansar, the banner in Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah’s (RA) hand. Sa‘d said, Abu Sufyan, today is the day of bloodshed; today even the sanctity of the Ka‘bah will be lifted. Last came the smallest band; the Prophet {{2}} and his Companions. Abu Sufyan (RA) told of Sa‘d’s words. The Prophet {{3}} said, Sa‘d has not spoken rightly; rather today is the day on which Allah will honour the Ka‘bah, the day on which the Ka‘bah will be clothed with its covering.{{4}}
blocks.21: The Prophet’s {{1}} green army began to pass. There, more than people, it was the iron armour that caught the eye. Abu Sufyan said, ‘Abbas, who are these? ‘Abbas (RA) said, the Messenger of Allah among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. Abu Sufyan said, by Allah, Abu al-Fadl, your nephew’s kingdom has become vast today! ‘Abbas said, Abu Sufyan, this is not kingship, it is prophethood. The Prophet {{2}} took the banner of the Ansar from the hand of Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and placed it in the hand of his son Qays. The banner moved from Sa‘d’s hand, but it did not move from the hands of the Ansar.{{3}}
blocks.22: On the day of entering Makkah the Prophet {{1}} announced,
blocks.24: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe; whoever throws down his weapon is safe; whoever keeps the door of his own house shut is safe.{{1}}
blocks.25: The man who at Badr, Uhud and the Trench had come with armies, his very house was made a refuge. The defeated leader’s head was kept high instead of bowed; so that his accepting of Islam would not turn into humiliation, but become a door of honour.
blocks.26: Sa‘d’s (RA) words came from the anger of war; after twenty years of oppression such words coming to the lips is not unnatural. But the one who is the leader corrected his companion’s angry words, without shaming him. Today is not a day of revenge; it is a day of honouring the Ka‘bah. ‘Abbas (RA) said to Abu Sufyan (RA), now run to your own people. Abu Sufyan ran to Makkah and announced in a loud voice, people of Quraysh, Muhammad has come with an army before which you have no strength to stand. Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe. His wife Hind came up, seized his moustache and cried, kill this fat one! What a bad bearer of news he is! Abu Sufyan said, ruin on you, do not fall for this woman’s deceit. Whoever enters my house is safe. The people said, how many of us will your house hold? He said, whoever sits with the door of his own house shut is also safe.{{1}}
blocks.27: Quraysh’s real reliance was Abu Sufyan’s word. Hearing such an announcement from the mouth of their own leader, no one else had anything to say. The tongue of that leader’s wife too was then fire. A few days later that same Hind would stand before the Prophet {{1}} and say, the honour of the people of your household is the dearest thing to me.

The part where the Prophet {{1}} said to ‘Amr ibn Salim ‘nusirta’ (you have been helped), al-Albani called weak (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 373), so it has not been kept in the dars.

footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 4276 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA); setting out in Ramadan, ten thousand, eight and a half years after arriving in Madinah).
footnotes.3: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 650–651 (the narration of al-Tabarani, Ibn Hisham 2/626–628, Zad al-Ma‘ad 2/150). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 1944, 4275, 4279 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA); breaking the fast at Kadid, raising the vessel to show people).
footnotes.5: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 2, Surah Yusuf 12:91, p. 116 (Taqi ‘Uthmani, checked by rendering the PDF). The confession of the brothers of Yusuf (AS).
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 2, Surah Yusuf 12:92, p. 116 (Taqi ‘Uthmani, checked by rendering the PDF). The Prophet {{1}} replied in the words of this very verse (al-Albani, Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 376: hasan; see the next note).
footnotes.7: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)). Al-Albani (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 376): hasan; Shu‘ayb Arna’ut (takhrij of Zad al-Ma‘ad 3/353): the chain is good. Umm Salamah’s intercession, the Prophet’s {{1}} first refusal, the oath of going out with his son’s hand, the reply ‘la tathriba’, the poem and the slap on the chest are in this narration. The part about Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith speaking the words of Yusuf’s brothers (12:91) is in Ibn Ishaq’s narration, on ‘Ali (RA)’s advice; Sirah-based. ‘Twenty years’ is according to Ibn Ishaq’s narration.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4280 (Hisham ibn ‘Urwah ← ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr). ⚠ This narration is mursal from ‘Urwah: ‘Urwah was a Tabi‘i, he was not even born at the time of the conquest of Makkah. Imam al-Bukhari brought it as mursal; Ibn Hajar said that most of it is established through other connected chains. The command to light separate fires is in Ibn Ishaq’s narration (Sirah-based).
footnotes.9: Part of the same Sahih al-Bukhari 4280 (making him stand in the pass, the tribes passing, Sa‘d’s ‘today is the day of bloodshed’ and the Prophet’s {{1}} reply). ⚠ ‘Urwah’s mursal portion; the sentence ‘today is the day of honouring the Ka‘bah’ al-Albani called separately weak because of its being mursal (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 380). But the general announcement of safety for the people of Makkah is established in the connected chain of Sahih Muslim 1780 (the next note).
footnotes.10: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 658 (Ibn Ishaq’s narration; in ‘Urwah’s mursal narration of Bukhari 4280 the banner of the Ansar and Abu Sufyan’s words are present; giving Sa‘d’s banner to Qays is in al-Rahiq, some have said it was given to Zubayr). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.11: Sahih Muslim 1780 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Fath Makkah). Al-Albani (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 377) also called it sahih through Ibn ‘Abbas’s chain.
footnotes.12: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 659 (Ibn Ishaq). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. This Hind bint ‘Utbah came a few days later to the Prophet {{1}} and accepted Islam (in the later part of the dars, Sahih al-Bukhari 7161).

quiz.q: In the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, whose ally was the Khuza‘ah tribe?
o: The chiefs of the Ghatafan tribe
quiz.e: Khuza‘ah was the Prophet’s ﷺ ally, Banu Bakr Quraysh’s.

quiz.q: Which tribe attacked Khuza‘ah?
quiz.e: Banu Bakr, with Quraysh’s help.

quiz.q: In the effort to renew the treaty, what advice did ‘Ali (RA) give Abu Sufyan?
o: To go to Abu Bakr and intercede again
To go to the Prophet ﷺ again and raise the matter
As a chief, to declare protection himself
quiz.e: Abu Sufyan announced it in the mosque; Quraysh said, he was only playing with you.

quiz.q: What is the lesson in comparing Quraysh’s breaking of the treaty with the Prophet’s ﷺ keeping his word at Hudaybiyah?
o: When you keep your word, time stands on your side
Making the treaty was itself a mistake
A treaty cannot be honoured from a weak position
It was proved that breaking a treaty is fine when one has power
quiz.e: One who breaks his word demolishes his own wall.

quiz.q: Someone has broken a treaty with me, though I had kept my word earlier; what does this dars say?
o: From now on I too will break
I will not make treaties at all
Keeping one’s word wins in the end
I will tell everyone and defame him all around
quiz.e: Quraysh broke it, and demolished their own wall.

quiz.q: ‘For one who himself breaks a treaty all doors are closed’; in which incident is this picture?
o: Abu Sufyan’s running about in Madinah
The reply to the Ansar’s weeping
quiz.e: Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Ali, none interceded.

quiz.q: How many Companions were in the expedition of the conquest of Makkah?
quiz.e: Ten thousand, according to Sahih al-Bukhari 4276.

quiz.q: In which month did the expedition of the conquest of Makkah take place?
quiz.e: In the month of Ramadan.

quiz.q: Near which spring did the Prophet ﷺ break his fast before everyone?
quiz.e: At Kadid.

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ raise the vessel and drink water before everyone at Kadid?
o: So that no one would feel shy to take the concession
To show that the fast is not obligatory
To force the Companions to break their fast, as a punishment
quiz.e: One action of the leader lightens the hardship of many.

quiz.q: Someone in the family is struggling to keep the rules even in illness, though there is a concession; what should a leader do?
o: Shame them by sternly ordering them to break the rule
Take the concession himself and make the way easy
quiz.e: The lesson of raising the vessel at Kadid.

quiz.q: What was Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith to the Prophet ﷺ?
o: A relative on the in-laws’ side
quiz.e: A paternal cousin, who for twenty years satirised him in verse.

quiz.q: Who interceded for Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith?
quiz.e: Umm Salamah (RA).

quiz.q: In the words of which prophet did the Prophet ﷺ reply to the cousin?
quiz.e: ‘No blame will be brought against you today.’

quiz.q: On hearing the poem, what did the Prophet ﷺ say to Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith?
o: You are the one who drove me out
Your poem has turned out beautiful
Now recite another poem to me
From today do not write poetry
quiz.e: He said it, slapping him on the chest.

quiz.q: What is expressed in first turning away Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and then accepting him?
o: He was compelled by Umm Salamah’s pressure
He was pleased on hearing the praise in the poem
quiz.e: To forgive does not mean to forget; it is to let go while remembering.

quiz.q: A relative who had satirised me for many years has come to ask forgiveness; what is the lesson of this dars?
o: Acknowledging the hurt and still drawing him to the chest
Humiliating him by recounting his old words before everyone
quiz.e: You are the one who drove me out; yet he drew him to his chest.

quiz.q: Seeing the fires of Marr al-Zahran, what did Abu Sufyan compare them to?
o: A forest fire on a distant mountain
quiz.e: It is like the fires of ‘Arafah.

quiz.q: Who else had come out with Abu Sufyan to get news?
o: Abu Jahl’s two sons and their men
quiz.e: Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa’.

quiz.q: Who was given the responsibility of keeping Abu Sufyan standing in the pass?
quiz.e: ‘Abbas (RA).

quiz.q: Who said ‘today is the day of bloodshed’?
quiz.e: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA), the banner-bearer of the Ansar.

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim, entering whose house was declared safe?
quiz.e: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe.

quiz.q: What is the significance of declaring Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge?
o: A strategy to keep him under watch
A plan to gather Quraysh in one place and imprison them
Protecting the honour of a defeated leader
quiz.e: So that accepting Islam would not become humiliation but a door of honour.

quiz.q: In reply to Sa‘d’s (RA) words ‘day of bloodshed’, what was the Prophet’s ﷺ position?
o: The day is not for revenge, it is for the honour of the Ka‘bah
Fully supporting Sa‘d’s words and becoming harsher
quiz.e: He corrected a companion’s angry words, without shaming him.

quiz.q: What could be the purpose of making Abu Sufyan stand in the pass and showing him the whole army pass?
o: To break the will to resist without bloodshed
To keep the army’s number secret
To punish him before sending him to Madinah as a prisoner
quiz.e: Seeing the strength, Quraysh gave up the thought of fighting.

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ himself was in the ‘smallest band’; what does this express?
o: A strategy arranged to deceive Quraysh
quiz.e: The biggest band was the Ansar’s; he was in the small band.

quiz.q: A leader of the opposing side has come over to my side; how is receiving him closer to the Prophet’s ﷺ example?
o: In a way that keeps his honour
Reminding him of his old mistakes
Seating him in the very back row for life
quiz.e: Declaring Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge.

quiz.q: Someone on the team has spoken harshly in anger; according to this dars, what should the leader do?
o: Correct the words without shaming him
Announce his expulsion from the team
quiz.e: The Prophet’s ﷺ conduct in reply to Sa‘d’s words.
